minimal_rule_inventory_effect.matching_test: Python anchored path predicates equivalent to these two directory rules, not Git check-ignore execution

semantics: Ignore rules affect untracked discovery only. Already tracked agent_outputs/selected evidence stays tracked and remains in future commits unless root explicitly changes the index; do not mass-untrack it.
Ignored raw files remain exactly on disk. This is neither deletion nor Git backup. Unpublished raw is not protected by Git push and needs separate verified data backup before any later cleanup.
Do not add /case/agent/, /case/agent/*/, evidence/, reference/, *.json, *.cfdproj, *.npy or *.npz blanket rules.
Do not replace existing /_tmp/ or logger ignore with deletion: ignored pinned runtimes, source snapshots and failed/partial scientific records may be required.
Existing tracked evidence is unaffected by any ignore rule, but new untracked evidence must stay visible or be deliberately curated with its manifest; no blanket evidence exclusion.

The current .gitignore already ignores broad scripts/, tests/, *.log, *.manifest and specific generator products. Preserve src/agent/tests and training/scripts exceptions; adding the two narrow rules needs no broad negation that would re-expose all raw evidence.
